title: A small drawn scene at the foot of the page that answers the pointer: star chart, lawn or koi pond
summary: One `aria-hidden` 2D canvas above the footer links, driven by a harness that owns size (backing store at `min(dpr, 2)`, reseeded from hashes on resize so the picture is the same on every load), the clock (the shared ticker, only while the scene is on screen and the tier is full) and the input (mouse and pen `pointermove`, `click` rather than `pointerdown` so a touch scroll leaves nothing), and three scene modules behind one contract: a star chart (one star per jittered `30 px` cell, the `5` nearest within `100 px` joined as a minimum spanning tree, a click holds them `5 s` and sends a `900 ms` shooting star), a lawn (a blade every `3 px`, sprung away from the pointer at `0.012 / 0.1` per 60 Hz frame within `90 px`, a click plants a flower that grows in `1.1 s`, at most `24`) and a koi pond (three fish on a 10-point spine that wander, come to a slow pointer, scatter from one faster than `0.9 px/ms` and race to a dropped pellet); a real button does by keyboard what a click does and a status line says it; reduced motion and static draw one settled frame and one more per input, with no loop
variants: a lawn the pointer parts, a click plants a flower (this, default)
a star chart: pointing joins the nearest stars, a click holds the constellation and sends a shooting star (the Star chart button, or `?scene=sky`)
a koi pond: the fish come to a slow pointer and scatter from a fast one, a click feeds them (the Koi pond button, or `?scene=pond`)
the same scene as a full-viewport hero: the canvas fills the first screen under a real heading, counts scale with the area, and what a click leaves stays for the visit
one of the scenes picked per load instead of one hard-coded, so a returning visitor meets a different close
